name: Borda
body:
Borda
CR 8

One fiery eye and a few patches of livid skin show in the gaps of the dirty, bloody bandages that wrap up this towering hag’s figure.

Rolling mist surrounds her as a shroud.

XP 4,800
NE Large monstrous humanoid (aquatic)
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft., sense fear; Perception +19; Aura horrific appearance (60 ft.)

DEFENSE

AC 21, touch 11, flat-footed 19 (+3 Dex, +9 natural, -1 size)
hp 105 (10d10+50)
Fort +8, Ref +10, Will +9; SR 19

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 30 ft.
Melee 2 claws +15 (1d6+6 plus grab) or rope +15/+15 (2d6+6 plus grab)
Special Attacks grab, rope master
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +13)

Constant—sense fear
At will—animate rope
3/day—fog cloud, rope trick, ropeweave
1/day—mind fog (DC 18)

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 17, Con 20, Int 16, Wis 15, Cha 16
Base Atk +10; CMB +17; CMD 29
Feats Alertness, Equipment Trick (rope), Improved Grapple, Improved Initiative, Iron Will
Skills Climb +19, Craft (ropemaking) +16, Intimidate +16, Perception +19, Stealth +16, Survival +15, Swim +19
Languages Common, Giant
SQ amphibious

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Horrific Appearance (Su)

The sight of a borda is so revolting that anyone within 60 feet (other than another hag) who sets eyes upon one must succeed on a DC 18 Fortitude save or instantly be weakened, taking 1d6 points of Strength damage. Creatures that are affected by this power or that successfully save against it cannot be affected again by the same hag’s horrific appearance for 24 hours. This is a mind-affecting effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Rope Master (Hex)

A borda can use all the tricks listed under Equipment Trick (rope) as if she matched the prerequisites for them. She also can try to grab an opponent when she inflicts damage with a rope attack.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate marshes, rivers, misty plains
Organization solitary or coven (3 hags of any kind)
Treasure standard (robe of infinite twine, other treasure)

A relative of the sea hag, the borda prefers to haunt the marshy areas next to rivers. She appears in dark hours and foggy days, kidnapping unwary passengers and children that she ties with her ropes and drags to her den to eat. Mothers use the borda to scare their children into behaving well:

Bordas resemble tall, wizened crones that seem to materialize out of the fog in a swamp. Her emaciated frame is covered in a ragged robe and coils of rope, with a ragged scrap of cloth bound over her eyes.

The embodiment of humanoid fears of swamps, the dangers that lurk within them, and drowning, bordas are solitary hags that dwell in swamps, marshes, or other wetland areas. Bordas were once common green hags, but a vile corruption elevates her to a new form and status by a supernatural connection to native fears focused on her and her homeland. There can be a only one borda in any given swamp, but only one, and each of them tends to refer to herself as the Borda, a creature unique to its local area.

Some say that a new borda will arise in the same locale if the current Borda dies, though others whisper that these hags are truly immortal and survive as long as her swamp remains.

True to the legends that surround her, the Borda is inimical to any trespassers in her domain, especially those that lose themselves in it by accident. She stalks and kills those she encounters, leaving their bound, drowned bodies to mummify in the peat beneath the swamp’s dark waters.

The borda’s body is covered in coiled rope, which she can magically form into nooses with which to catch and strangle her victims or drag them under the water with her to kill at her leisure. She also has a hag’s claws and her bite is venomous like many of the inhabitants of her home.

Borda Covens

When a borda joins a coven, the coven adds acid fog, solid fog, and wall of mist to its spell-like abilities, and any member within 1 mile of the borda gains her sense fear ability.

A borda has a magical connection to her swamp home. Even without use of her eyes, she is aware of everything in her immediate area. Further abroad, the borda’s sense of her domain is vaguer. If an intruder enters the swamp, she will eventually become aware of it, knowing the general direction in which the intruder lies. This means the borda, if so inclined, will eventually find someone if they are within her domain. The closer they are, the more quickly she will find them.

Unlike other hags, a borda is content with a solitary life in her domain and does not seek to form a coven with other hags. Only when forced by the greatest necessity, typically the threat of powerful heroes invading her swamp, will the borda reach out to her sisters to gain power by forming a triad with two other hags (typically green hags).

Occasionally, a borda will terrorize a victim, only to allow them to escape, or choose a single victim in a group to leave alive. She knows they will return home to tell their harrowing tale of their encounter with her, instilling fear in most, and enticing the brave or foolhardy into her domain as her next victims.

The Borda’s Lair

The borda’s lair is typically located deep within the swamp that is her domain. It can be a partially (or fully) sunken ruin, grotto, moss-encrusted grove of ancient willows, or flooded cave. The lair will be enshrouded with fog, with the mummified corpses of victims hidden beneath the still waters. Dangerous swamp creatures—venomous snakes, stirges, giant insects, or others—lurk within the borda’s lair.

REGIONAL EFFECTS

The region containing the borda’s lair is adversely affected by her sinister presence, which creates one or more of the following effects:

Travelers within 10 miles of the lair find themselves disoriented and prone to becoming lost or wandering into danger. Creatures take a -2 penalty on Survival checks to navigate the area or to recognize hazards are made at disadvantage.
A constant fog lightly obscures the land within 6 miles of the lair, causing a -2 penalty on visual Perception checks to notice things more than 30 feet away.
Local wildlife and creatures living within 6 miles of the lair are automatically hostile when encountered. If there is a chance of random encounters in the area, double the chances of such an encounter occurring.
